metadata.description: Sample event demonstrating multi-source accounts (historical vs literary)

summary.zh: 孙刘联军在赤壁击败曹操水军，阻止曹操统一天下，奠定三国鼎立格局
summary.en: Sun-Liu alliance defeated Cao Cao's naval forces at Red Cliffs, preventing unification and establishing basis for Three Kingdoms division

sequence_of_events.description: Cao Cao advances south after conquering Jingzhou
sequence_of_events.source_citation: Book of Wei, Biography of Emperor Wu

sequence_of_events.description: Sun Quan and Liu Bei form alliance against Cao Cao
sequence_of_events.source_citation: Book of Wu, Biography of Sun Quan; Book of Shu, Biography of Zhuge Liang

sequence_of_events.description: Huang Gai proposes fire attack strategy
sequence_of_events.source_citation: Book of Wu, Biography of Huang Gai

sequence_of_events.description: Fire ships sent into Cao's fleet, causing massive destruction
Cao Cao retreats northward, abandons campaign
sequence_of_events.source_citation: Book of Wei, Biography of Emperor Wu

casualties.cao_forces: Heavy losses to fire and subsequent retreat

outcome.strategic_impact: Prevented Cao Cao from unifying China under Wei control

key_factors: Alliance between Sun Quan and Liu Bei
Cao Cao's forces unfamiliar with naval warfare
Northerners suffering from disease in southern climate

controversies.question: Exact location of battle
controversies.positions: Multiple sites claim to be Red Cliffs

chapter_titles.zh: 宴长江曹操赋诗 锁战船北军用武
chapter_titles.en: Cao Cao's Banquet and Poetry at Yangtze

chapter_titles.zh: 七星坛诸葛祭风 三江口周瑜纵火
chapter_titles.en: Zhuge Liang Prays for Wind, Zhou Yu Sets Fire

chapter_titles.zh: 诸葛亮智算华容 关云长义释曹操
chapter_titles.en: Zhuge Liang's Stratagem at Huarong, Guan Yu Releases Cao Cao

summary.zh: 诸葛亮借东风，庞统献连环计，黄盖诈降，周瑜火烧赤壁，大败曹军；关羽华容道义释曹操
summary.en: Zhuge Liang summons east wind, Pang Tong suggests chain stratagem, Huang Gai feigns surrender, Zhou Yu burns fleet at Red Cliffs; Guan Yu releases Cao Cao at Huarong Road

dramatic_elements.element: Zhuge Liang prays for east wind on altar

dramatic_elements.historical_basis: Ships may have been chained, but Pang Tong's role uncertain
dramatic_elements.purpose: Add intrigue and demonstrate strategic brilliance

dramatic_elements.historical_basis: Huang Gai did lead fire attack, surrender ruse likely embellished

dramatic_elements.element: Guan Yu releases Cao Cao at Huarong Road
dramatic_elements.historical_basis: No historical record of this encounter
dramatic_elements.purpose: Demonstrate Guan Yu's honor and gratitude (repaying past favor)

literary_themes: Unity against common enemy (联合抗敌)
Supernatural elements showing mandate of heaven

famous_quotes.speaker: Cao Cao

quote.en: If Zhou Yu exists, why must Zhuge Liang exist too?

famous_quotes.context: Zhou Yu's jealousy of Zhuge Liang's talent (actually from later chapters)
famous_quotes.note: Often misattributed to Red Cliffs context

historical_core: Battle occurred in 208/209 CE at Red Cliffs
Cao Cao retreated north after defeat

literary_additions.rationale: Elevate Zhuge Liang to legendary status
Create narrative tension and showcase intelligence
Demonstrate moral virtue and honor above practical concerns

divergence_analysis.note: Core events accurate, but heavily embellished with fictional details
most_fictional_aspects: Zhuge Liang's central role (historically Zhou Yu led campaign)

immediate_impact: Prevented Cao Cao from conquering south
Established defensive line along Yangtze River
long_term_impact: Set stage for Three Kingdoms period (220-280)
significance.historical_assessment: One of the most decisive battles in Chinese history
significance.cultural_impact: One of most famous battles in Chinese culture, subject of countless adaptations

name.en: Cao Cao's Southern Campaign to Jingzhou

related_events.note: Sun and Liu divided conquered territory
Cao Cao's defense in the north during same period
